Abhang: design audit

Audited on a physical Redmi Note 11 (2201117TI, Android 16, 1080×2400, density 460) running the installed debug build, plus the Compose source. Eight real screenshots were captured; light and dark themes and maximum reading size were exercised. The orange identity stays. Every recommendation below keeps the saffron palette and light-orange accents.

11 / 20Acceptable: significant work needed
8P1 · major

4P3 · polish

What was captured

Audit health score

DimensionScoreKey finding
Accessibility2 / 4White-on-saffron bar is 3.8:1; unlabeled अ−/अ+; low-contrast counts; two stacked font-scale controls.
Performance2 / 4First search stalls 1–4 s on a mid-range phone and shows a false "nothing found"; 4.5 MB JSON parsed on every cold start.
Appearance & theming2 / 4Dark mode puts a glaring amber bar on a dark screen; light nav bar stays in dark mode; text fields are off-palette lavender.
Platform conformance3 / 4Material 3 structure and Back work. Missing: launcher icon, edge-to-edge, DayNight window theme.
Adaptivity2 / 4Reading controls take about 17% of a portrait screen and far more in landscape; no wide-screen text measure.

Verdict: it reads as a native Material app, not a web port, and the Devanagari typography is good. The weak spots are (1) trust and findability in search, (2) a reading view that ignores the structure of a verse and spends its space on controls, (3) dark mode, which is the mode used in dim bhajan rooms, and (4) contrast of the orange itself.

Pick what to implement

0 selected

Systemic patterns

  • Orange is doing two jobs. #E65100 is both the fill colour (fine) and the text/bar colour (too light for text). Split it: keep #E65100 for fills, switches, indicators; add a deeper burnt saffron #B93C00 (white on it 5.7:1, on cream 5.4:1) for the app bar, headings and small orange text. The look stays orange.
  • Defaults leak through. Default TextField colours, default Switch, default Light window theme and default launcher icon are the places the app stops looking like itself.
  • Controls are global, content is local. Font size buttons sit on every screen but matter on one; search sits as an icon but is the product's key feature.
  • The text is treated as a string. The reading view renders the abhang body as a paragraph, losing the couplet, refrain and signature structure the corpus already encodes.

What is working well

  • Warm cream and saffron palette is cohesive and instantly reads devotional without ornament.
  • Google Sans in the bundle covers all 128 Devanagari codepoints (verified from the font's cmap), so Marathi renders in one consistent face, not a device fallback. Conjuncts and matras render cleanly at 22sp and at the 44sp maximum.
  • Reading view line height (1.6) and verse size (22sp) are comfortable; title, author and body hierarchy is clear.
  • Search and category filtering run off the main thread; lists use LazyColumn with stable keys; touch targets in lists and buttons meet 48dp.
  • Keep-screen-on in the reading view is exactly the right instinct for singing from the phone.
  • Filtering by abhang number (Devanagari or ASCII digits) and phonetic Latin search are genuine differentiators once surfaced.
  • A real dark scheme exists; it needs refining, not building.
